description:
05-11's own decimal-data-error incident scenario (docs/part05/05-11-decimal-data-error.md), executed end to end for the first time: C0511S (src/qclsrc/c0511s.clp) plants JUNO='C05119' into JUCHUD with a CPYF FMTOPT(*NOCHK)-corrupted JUSU (raw bytes of 'ABCDE', invalid zoned decimal), then a CALL chain reaching za0500.rpg's own `SUB JUSU AVAIL` line is expected to raise a decimal-data-error citing that specific statement, letting VFYLOG settle whether it is MCH1202 (this lesson's own name for the scenario) or RPG0907 (already observed for an unrelated cause, see below) or something else.

Revision 2 (this pass): rewritten after two reviewers found the first version would very likely have spent its one connection without reaching the scenario at all, or without being able to tell its result apart from an unrelated bug. Both findings were confirmed by re-reading primary sources (rpg400ref.txt, za0500.rpg's own F-specs, db/v1/juchum.pf's DDS, docs/probes.md) before writing this revision - see the two 'FIXED' paragraphs below.

FIXED (docs/probes.md citation, reviewer 1's framing finding): docs/probes.md's `part05-ju0900c-baseline` entry (confirmed 2026-09-27, same day as this design) already states, from a real CALL of the as-shipped JU0900C/ZA0500 chain against the untouched sample DB, that OPM RPG/400 (ZA0500 is CRTRPGPGM, not ILE) reports decimal-data errors through its OWN message class `RPG0907` ("ZA0500 8100 decimal-data error in field (C G S D F)."), and records `MCH1202` as 'おそらく MI/ILEレベルの等価物であり、OPM RPG/400からは自分自身のメッセージ体系で報告される' - i.e. OPM RPG/400 is not expected to ever surface MCH1202 itself. That entry explicitly instructs: '05-11(MCH1202)のマニフェスト設計時は、この接続で確定した実際のメッセージID(RPG0907)とエスケープ経路を踏まえること.' The same entry also establishes, by cross-referencing the compiler's own statement-number listing against za0500.rpg's source, that for THIS UNMODIFIED FILE the compiler's statement number is the source line number times 100 (its statement 8100 = line 81, `N90 AVAIL COMP MINQTY`). Applying that same rule to the lines this manifest actually cares about (see expected/notes.md for the full table): line 64 (JUCHUD's own I-spec for JUSU, where OPM RPG converts the corrupted bytes at record-selection time) is statement 6400; line 80 (`N90 SUB JUSU AVAIL`, the arithmetic use of the corrupted JUSU) is statement 8000; line 93 (`O JUSU 21`, the QSYSPRT output edit of JUSU) is statement 9300; line 81 (`N90 AVAIL COMP MINQTY`, ticket 1's own bug) is statement 8100. So this manifest's central open question is no longer framed as 'which message ID fires' (RPG0907 is now the odds-on favorite for ANY decimal-data error out of OPM RPG/400, MCH1202 or not) but as 'which STATEMENT NUMBER the decimal-data error names' - 6400, 8000 or 9300 all confirm the corrupted-JUSU hypothesis this lesson is actually about (they only differ in when the bad byte pattern is actually acted on); statement 8100 would be unexpected here since JU0900T (below) removes ticket 1's MINQTY mismatch. See verify/part05-mch1202-corrupt/expected/notes.md for the full statement-number table and how to read VFYLOG against it - including the important caveat that 'no decimal-data error at all' is NOT the same as 'confirmed harmless': ZA0500's own QSYSPRT output has never been confirmed to reach this harness's captured stdout, so a silent run cannot yet be told apart from C05119 never being reached.

FIXED (reviewer 2's correctness finding: the original design would very likely never reach `SUB JUSU AVAIL` for C05119 at all, and even if it did, could not tell the corrupted-JUSU error apart from ticket 1's unrelated MINQTY bug): re-derived from primary sources instead of only from JUCHUD's own OPNQRYF order (which is all the original design checked).
  1. za0500.rpg's F-spec for JUCHUM (`FJUCHUM IS F 26 DISK`) leaves position 31 (Record Address Type) BLANK. rpg400ref.txt (work/design/refs/rpg400ref.txt, 'Position 31 (Record Address Type)', ~line 6707): 'If this position is blank for a keyed file, the records are retrieved in arrival sequence.' db/v1/juchum.pf's own DDS DOES declare `A K JUNO` (a keyed file), but ZA0500 itself does not open it by that key (no OPNQRYF override for JUCHUM anywhere in JU0900C, unlike JUCHUD) - so ZA0500 reads JUCHUM in physical/arrival order, which after TXRESET + C0511S's plain SQL INSERT is J00001..J00008 (TXRESET's load order) THEN C05119 (inserted last, appended to the end). Since the M1/MR matching cycle in za0500.rpg (`C 01 MR GOTO PROCLN` / `GOTO SKPALL`) only enters the CHAIN/SUB/COMP block on a genuinely MATCHED (01+MR) pair, and JUCHUD's own OPNQRYF-ascending C05119 primary record would be compared against JUCHUM's arrival-order-first J00001 secondary record ('C05119' < 'J00001'), the ORIGINAL design's C05119 primary read would most likely land as an unmatched 01-only record (GOTO SKPALL, `SUB JUSU AVAIL` never executed) - the real match would occur later, at J00001, reproducing part05-ju0900c-baseline's own already-observed RPG0907/MINQTY finding instead of anything new.
     FIX: a new CL step (CLRJUCHUM, below) unconditionally `RUNSQL SQL('DELETE FROM &LIB/JUCHUM')`s ALL rows out of JUCHUM (not just JUNO='C05119') AFTER TXRESET but BEFORE C0511S's own CALL. C0511S then inserts exactly one JUCHUM row (C05119), so by the time JU0900T/ZA0500 run, JUCHUM contains exactly one record. With only one secondary key in existence, the matching-record cycle is forced to compare EVERY JUCHUD primary key against that same single 'C05119' key until it is matched-and-consumed or passed (Pk > Sk consumes it unmatched); given JUCHUD's own OPNQRYF ascending-JUNO order genuinely does place 'C05119' before 'J00001' (EBCDIC X'C3' < X'D1', unchanged from the original reasoning and not challenged by either reviewer), the very first JUCHUD primary read equals the only JUCHUM key, so `01+MR` fires deterministically on cycle 1 and ZA0500 reaches the code that reads/uses the corrupted JUSU against that row. IMPORTANT: this still DEPENDS on the OPNQRYF-ascending-order assumption above, same as the original design - isolating JUCHUM removes the (reviewer-found, real) arrival-order problem on the JUCHUM side, it does not make this manifest independent of JUCHUD's own read order. If that assumption were ever wrong (JUCHUD not genuinely ascending by this comparison), the lone JUCHUM secondary record would be consumed as an unmatched secondary (or trigger a matching-sequence error) before the primary ever reaches 'C05119', and the corrupted row would still be skipped - this residual dependency is called out again in this manifest's own remaining-risks note (see the workflow's final report), not asserted away here. JUCHUD itself is deliberately NOT wiped, so the third `collect` step below (an ordinary row's JUSU for comparison) still has real rows to read.
     Considered and rejected: RGZPFM FILE(&LIB/JUCHUM) KEYFILE(*FILE) (to reorder JUCHUM onto its own DDS key) - work/design/refs/cl_commands_75.txt has no RGZPFM entry and no other file in work/design/refs/ documents its KEYFILE parameter's exact syntax, so per this session's own 'unconfirmed new keyword' rule this was avoided in favor of the DELETE-based isolation above, which reuses an idiom (RUNSQL DELETE FROM &LIB/<table>) already proven working elsewhere in this same harness (clgen.mjs's own VFYLOG/VFYSPL housekeeping, C0511S's own per-key deletes).
     Considered and rejected: bypass JU0900C entirely and CALL a verification-only ZA0500 clone directly (part05-qcmdexc-runtime's ZA0510V precedent) - kept as a documented fallback only; the JUCHUM-isolation fix above lets this manifest keep using the real JU0900C call chain (closer to how a learner would actually trigger this incident) while still being deterministic.
  2. Even once `SUB JUSU AVAIL` is reached, the as-shipped JU0900C (`&MINQTY TYPE(*DEC) LEN(3 0)`) still disagrees with ZA0500's `*ENTRY PLIST` (`MINQTY 5,0`) - 05-13 ticket 1's own bug, already confirmed (part05-ju0900c-baseline) to raise its OWN RPG0907 at statement 8100 (`AVAIL COMP MINQTY`) on ANY row that reaches that far, independent of JUSU. Calling the as-shipped JU0900C here would leave a genuine ambiguity for any row that reaches COMP MINQTY without first raising an error at SUB JUSU AVAIL (e.g. if OPM RPG/400 turns out NOT to raise a decimal error at SUB for this corruption). FIX: this manifest now compiles solutions/05-13/ju0900c-ticket1.clp (`&MINQTY LEN(5 0)`, the 05-13 model answer - the RPG side, za0500.rpg, is left as-shipped) under the distinct object name JU0900T (matching the ZA0500T3/ZA0510V naming precedent for a verification-only variant compiled alongside, not over, the as-shipped object), and CALLs JU0900T instead of JU0900C. This removes the MINQTY confound entirely, so ANY decimal-data error this connection observes on the C05119 row is attributable to the corrupted JUSU, not to ticket 1 - the statement-number check above becomes a confirmation, not the only line of defense.

Blast radius (bigger than the original design, note for future manifests): CLRJUCHUM leaves &LIB/JUCHUM holding ONLY the C05119 row after this connection (not TXRESET's normal J00001..J00008, and not merely 'the normal 8 plus 1' as the original design left it) - JUCHUD is untouched apart from C05119's own addition. This is a strictly bigger change to shared state than the original design's own already-documented 'leaves C05119 sitting in &LIB, run TXRESET again before any future part05-* manifest' note (verify/part05-13-tickets/expected/notes.md's own '前提(2)' section already defends against the ORIGINAL, smaller version of this by running TXRESET first - that defense still works against this bigger version too, since TXRESET restores JUCHUM's full data unconditionally). This manifest deliberately does NOT clean up after itself for the same hang-risk-last reason as the original design (the CALL to JU0900T must stay last).

JUBADD's role (src/legacy/qddssrc/jubadd.pf, read in full for this manifest): a 27-byte record, field-for-field identical to JUCHUD's own JUCHDR format, except JUSU is 5A (character) instead of JUCHUD's 5S 0 (zoned decimal) - it exists ONLY so CPYF FMTOPT(*NOCHK) has a type-mismatched source to copy from; nothing else in this curriculum ever reads or writes it. C0511S never CALLs anything against JUBADD itself.

Why TXRESET runs FIRST (via the already-hardware-confirmed &LIB/TXRESET LIB(&LIB) *CMD form, docs/probes.md's part06-0509-procs-files/part07-05-checkpoint confirmations): this manifest cannot assume &LIB's JUCHUD/JUCHUM are still in their db/data/load_v1.sql starting state (several other part05-*/part05-13-tickets manifests may have connected to this same dev-role library before this one). TXRESET only restores DATA (RUNSQLSTM against db/data/reset_v1.sql then load_v1.sql) - it does not touch JUBADD or any compiled *PGM, and it does not need to know C0511S exists (matches the lesson's own 実機メモ: 'TXRESET restores DATA only').

Why a small helper CL (src/c0511run.clp) CALLs C0511S instead of a plain CALL PGM(&LIB/C0511S) PARM('&LIB' ' ') step: C0511S's &CLONEDIR *ENTRY PLIST parameter is LEN(200), but a literal typed directly into a CALL command's PARM() is only blank-padded up to 32 bytes (docs/probes.md's own finding - the same reason tools/qclsrc/txsetup.clp/txreset.clp/txlegacy.clp all grew *CMD wrappers, and the same reason verify/part05-txlegacy-exec/src/txlegrun.clp exists for TXLEGACY's own LIB(...) *CMD invocation). c0511run.clp instead DCLs its own LEN(200) &CLONEDIR variable (left blank) and passes IT by reference, which carries its own full declared length regardless of contents. See that file's own header comment for the full reasoning. UNVERIFIED: this exact call (C0511RUN -> C0511S, including C0511S's own CURUSER-based CLONEDIR default) has never been run on real hardware before this manifest.

Why C0511S needs its OWN CLONEDIR-relative copy of jubadd.pf staged in the IFS (the sh/MKTREE + sh/TOSTMF-JUBADD steps below, mirroring verify/part05-txlegacy-exec's already-reviewed CPYTOSTMF technique): C0511S's own Step 1 does an UNCONDITIONAL `CPYFRMSTMF FROMSTMF(&CLONEDIR/src/legacy/qddssrc/jubadd.pf) ... STMFCCSID(1208)` with no step-local MONMSG of its own - only the program-level `MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000) EXEC(GOTO CMDLBL(FAILSAFE))` at the very top would catch a failure there, aborting C0511S before it ever reaches the JUBADD-exists-so-continue logic. Part 5 is still draft-only (not yet on main), so this manifest cannot assume src/legacy/qddssrc/jubadd.pf is really there already on PUB400's real clone. The two sh steps below place a genuinely CCSID-1208-tagged/encoded copy of it at the exact CLONEDIR-relative path C0511S's own CPYFRMSTMF expects.

ZA0500 (as-shipped, ticket 1's own MINQTY bug intentionally left alone on the RPG side - only JU0900T's CL side is widened, per the FIX above) and JU0900T are recompiled fresh here (REPLACE(*YES), DLTPGM-first) - self-containment, same reasoning part05-ju0900c-baseline already uses for ZA0500/JU0900C. RUNMODE stays '*TEST' so ZAIKOM's real quantities are never mutated. MONMSG on the two genuinely-new-code CALL steps (RUNC0511S, RUNJU0900T) matches part05-ju0900c-baseline's own broad net (CPF0000/MCH0000/RPG0000).

Evidence collected: VFYLOG's own automatic per-connection job-log dump (should show a decimal-data error citing statement 8000 per the FIXED reasoning above - read its exact message ID AND statement number, do not assume MCH1202 just because that is this lesson's name for the scenario), plus a safe HEX-only collect step (JUNO/JULINE/HEX(JUSU) only, no raw JUSU column) as the FIRST collect so the single piece of evidence this whole batch exists to gather survives even if a raw SELECT of the corrupted JUSU itself errors out (05-11's own lesson text warns this may happen - 'その場合はHEX(JUSU)だけをSELECTし直してください', which this harness cannot do interactively mid-connection), followed by the fuller best-effort query (with raw JUSU) reusing 05-11's own src/sql/05-11-hex.sql query verbatim, then a comparison against an ordinary JUCHUD row's HEX(JUSU) (still available - JUCHUD itself was not wiped), then a cheap cross-check that RUNMODE='*TEST' left ZAIKOM's P00001 quantity untouched. Prerequisite: TXSETUP has already built the sample DB in this library, same prerequisite as every other part05-* manifest - run from a branch where src/qclsrc/c0511s.clp, solutions/05-13/ju0900c-ticket1.clp and docs/part05/05-11-decimal-data-error.md all exist, not main.

steps.label: CPC0511RUN
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511RUN)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511RUN) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(C0511RUN) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPC0511S
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511S)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511S) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(C0511S) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPJU0900T
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900T)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900T) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(JU0900T) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPZA0500
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTRPGPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGSRC) SRCMBR(ZA0500) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.sql: SELECT JUNO, JULINE, HEX(JUSU) AS JUSU_HEX FROM &LIB/JUCHUD WHERE JUNO = 'C05119'
SELECT JUNO, JULINE, JUSHO, JUSU, HEX(JUSU) AS JUSU_HEX, JUTNK FROM &LIB/JUCHUD WHERE JUNO = 'C05119'
SELECT JUNO, JULINE, JUSU, HEX(JUSU) AS JUSU_HEX FROM &LIB/JUCHUD WHERE JUNO <> 'C05119' FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY
SELECT ZASHO, ZASU, ZAUPD FROM &LIB/ZAIKOM WHERE ZASHO = 'P00001'
